description:
Found while reviewing fz-3ul.3 against the BEAM. The handler miss (a try whose rescue/catch clauses all miss) and the after handler re-raise by calling Kernel.raise_kind/2, resolved by name through the calling module's namespace (body.rs reraise_block -> call_raising_block). That forces raise_kind/2 to be public auto-imported Kernel surface Elixir does not have, and because it takes a kind atom from anyone, fz_raise_kind parses the atom and invents a :badarg error for an unknown kind.

The BEAM has the same primitive but not the same door: erlang:throw/1, erlang:exit/1 and erlang:error/1,2 are fixed-class BIFs behind Kernel's throw/exit/raise; the try handler is a case over {Class, Value, RawStk} whose fallthrough is the compiler primop raise(RawStk, Value), which hands back exactly what the landing pad delivered. Nothing in Kernel takes a class; erlang:raise/3 lives in the runtime's module.

Build: LastResort gains a re-raise variant, "continue the arrived raise with the plan's first two inputs (kind, value)". The handler dispatch is built with that last resort and no miss_block; the after handler is a dispatch with no rows and the same last resort, so both handlers have the BEAM's shape (a case whose fallthrough is the re-raise). The plan's Fail lowers to a Term::Reraise { kind, value } terminator in native codegen (fz_reraise, then continue_after_raise) and to the runtime's re-raise in the interpreter (then after_panic), beside Term::Raise. The kind is the atom the handler was delivered; a kind the runtime never delivered is unreachable by construction and is an assertion, not a :badarg raise. throw/1 and exit/1 call fixed-kind externs fz_throw/fz_exit the way raise/2 calls fz_raise. Delete Kernel.raise_kind/2 (def, @doc, @spec, the lib/runtime.fz entry, the kernel.fz module-doc mention), extern fz_raise_kind and its :badarg branch, reraise_block's DirectCall and call_raising_block if it loses its last user. reraise/2 stays panic(exception) until fz-3ul.5 gives it a stacktrace to carry.

Acceptance (interp, run, build):
- fixtures 00733-00739, 00750-00757, 00758-00793 pass unchanged; in particular the catch fixtures (a throw that no clause takes reaches the outer catch as a throw; exit(:normal)/exit(:shutdown)/exit({:shutdown, n}) through a try ... after end main with status 0/0/n; an uncaught throw prints ** (throw) v, exit 1).
- grep -rn 'raise_kind' lib src runtime .agent is empty.
- a program calling raise_kind(:throw, 1) gets the ordinary undefined-function diagnostic.
- fz.runtime.raise telemetry for a re-raise through an after is unchanged: two events, the re-raise one frame shallower, same kind on both.
- unit tests: fz_throw/fz_exit deliver kinds throw/exit; fz_reraise continues with the delivered kind; the :badarg test is deleted with the branch; the lowering test asserts the handler dispatch's last resort is the re-raise and miss_block is None.
- .agent/docs/exceptions.md (kinds table, 'throw/1, exit/1 and raise_kind/2 are plain fz code' paragraph, handler-miss and after bullets, 'Where it lives'), dispatch-matrix.md ~1185 (LastResort), runtime-telemetry.md ~92, lib/kernel.fz docs updated in the same commit; no pin or golden moves.
- gate green as in the epic.
title: The handler miss re-raises as a terminator, and raise_kind/2 leaves Kernel
